channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Nov 5–11
item.description: The biggest thing to watch this week is the TMVOA Board of Directors kicking off its three-meeting 2027 budget cycle on Thursday, November 6 — they'll be reviewing the completed 2025 audit and getting a first look at next year's draft budget, so this is the moment to start paying attention if Mountain Village assessments or services affect you. The regional intergovernmental meeting on Sunday, November 9, brings Telluride, Mountain Village, Ophir, Norwood, and the county together for a cross-jurisdictional large-projects update — the kind of session where things that matter to the whole valley get aired quietly. On the lighter side, the week has plenty going on, from the Adult Spelling Bee Friday night to the Wildbelly Fermentation Fest Saturday and a Free Legal Clinic Tuesday.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] TMVOA Board of Directors Budget Meeting #1 — 2026-11-06
item.description:
tmvoa • 2026-11-06
The Telluride Mountain Village Owners Association opens its three-meeting budget cycle for 2027 with this first session on November 6. The bulk of the afternoon goes to two substantive items: a presentation of the completed 2025 audit and tax return by CLA (Clifton, Larson, Allen LP), and a first look at the 2027 draft budget. Two more budget sessions follow — November 19 and December 3 — before the Members Meeting on December 17, where the budget is expected to be finalized. Routine minutes approval and public comment round out the agenda.
⚡ Why it matters: First look at TMVOA 2027 draft budget and 2025 audit affects every Mountain Village owner's assessments.

item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride Immersive Sound Journey with Dustin Wells In-Person An immersive sound journey is a live musical experience you take lying down. Musician and sound ceremony artist Dustin Wells surrounds the room with sacred instruments — gongs, shamanic drums, singing bowls, crystal bowls, wind chimes — woven live with synths, guitar, and voice into a single two-hour soundscape. The journey moves through a deliberate arc, from settling in to full sound to a quiet return, designed to guide the nervous system out of fight-or-flight and into the state where the body does its own healing. Come as you are; leave with what you came for. · Please arrive 30 minutes early to find your spot and get comfortable. · Suggested: bring what makes the floor feel like home — a yoga mat, pillow, blanket, or eye mask. Guests lie down if there's room, or sit as needed. …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Intergovernmental Meeting - Nov 09 2026 — 2026-11-09
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-11-09
San Miguel County hosts this intergovernmental work session with representatives from Telluride, Mountain Village, Ophir, Norwood, and the county itself. The session opens with a regional large-projects update covering all five jurisdictions — the kind of cross-entity check-in that surfaces where development pressures and infrastructure needs are colliding across the valley. From there, County Emergency Manager Shannon Armstrong presents an updated Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan process, followed by an update on Indigenous tribal relations from Marya Stark, lead for the Indigenous People's working group. The session closes with a presentation from Elaine Demas of the Telluride Foundation on a shared inter-jurisdictional housing framework being structured to qualify under Proposition 123 — the state affordable housing program that comes with real money attached, if the jurisdictions can demonstrate the required coordination. No formal action can be taken at a work session.
⚡ Why it matters: Regional large-projects update surfaces cross-jurisdictional development and infrastructure pressures affecting the whole valley.

item.title: [Wed, Nov 11] Dee William's 2026 Volunteer of the Year Celebration
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Wright Opera House, Ouray The Telluride Foundation is proud to announce Dee Williams as the recipient of the 2026 Volunteer of the Year Award. Dee has provided decades of service and leadership in Ouray County. Dee's many contributions include helping launch the Home Trust of Ouray County (HTOC), where she served for four years on the board and continues to volunteer as a coordinator for the 10K Fourth of July fundraiser and Home Tour. She also helped to found the Ouray Nordic Council and established cross-country ski tracks at Ironton. When the Wright Opera House was at risk of being sold and converted into condominiums, Dee stepped up with others to form the Friends of the Wright Opera House. She helped raise funds and preserve the historic building as a nonprofit—ensuring it would remain a special place for the community. …
